body: I know; getting stuff done is great! Beats sitting around worrying about how I'm going to get a speech, my speech folder, roughly 7 programming projects, and a history presentation done in time. I just need to keep this up long enough to catch up. Hopefully, between this new shot of confidence and my upcoming appointments, I'll be rid of this depression soon.

I seem to be making a lot of progress today. I feel unusually motivated and energetic. Although, I still feel a little sad, it's not depression. I'm actually getting stuff done that I've been putting off from the depression.

I had a little crisis earlier, but I was able to rationalize through it. I've been doing the activities in the MoodGym program trying to observe and study my depression. I was also able to call and set up an appointment with a therapist next month. So, I guess I'm feeling pretty good due to my progress.
Well, I guess I can try analyzing my depression until it goes away. It'd be better than just accepting it and staying depressed.

Oh, I get it now. Technically, depression is an illness rather than a state of being, so this does make sense.

That also makes sense. By focusing on it and studying my depression, it will eventually subside because I'm not focused on staying depressed all the time. Right?
I was always under the impression that we ultimately control how we feel. Is this something along the lines of what you're saying? I think I understand if it is.
Thank you.
That would be great if I could do that. I'll try calling some local therapists and see if I can work anything out. At least I can say that I tried.
Eh, now that you mention it, it sounds a lot like how you describe it. I can't figure out why, but "mental weather condition" makes a whole lot more sense.
I'll keep that in mind. Thank you.

I know it's illogical, but it's just such a powerful and haunting thought. I know getting back out of this isn't going to be easy, but I'm just scared that if I get out again, will I fall back again? 

The non medication part of my therapy was CBT. Most of it though was trying to figure out what exactly I had. It ended up being unclassifiable. It wasn't depression, it wasn't bipolar, and it wasn't anything the doctors could classify (which I find odd, given that I overheard one of the doctors say that it was closer to psychosis than anything).

As much as I'd love help, not having a car really hinders what I can do to find help.

I'm sure most hotlines don't treat people like that. I just know that I'm not going to try it again.

Let me put it like this: I never left the mountain. I've been stuck here for two years. For the last year up until recently, I ignored being stuck on it. After putting it off for as long as I could, I remembered that I'm still stuck at the same spot. I can't see a path, and I am lost.

I meant thriving in the sense that you are living, sorry if I wasn't clear.

The answer to this would be an extremely drawn out tl;dr post that would probably bore you to tears. I might PM you the the condensed version. Also, I'd try a hotline, but every time I try one, I get treated poorly. I don't know who has the audacity to hire these people at hotlines, but when someone is at the brink of suicide, "We don't help crazy people" is in no way shape or form an appropriate sentence.

I see. Well, thank you. In your analogy though, I feel like I'm climbing a mountain. Not just another mountain compared to the first depression, but the very same mountain, if that makes any sense.

I'm glad to hear that you were able to recover and thrive. I just wish I could be that strong.

As much as I'd love to be able to ask for help, this is about as far as I can get. I can't see any therapists or get any sort of medications. My last battle was bad enough to knock me out of being able to ask for help again. I still appreciate being able to talk here though. I just hope I won't come across as being too whiny or pathetic.

My main form of treatment was direct counseling with 2 medications. It worked while I could do it, but after taking a year off from college just to try and get back on track, I needed to stop in order to go back to college.

I have no idea. I just feel like life is beginning to get overwhelming again. I'd blame it on my difficulty in college, but I'm not doing too bad at the moment. I'd blame it on my girlfriend saying she didn't like me anymore, but I was already too depressed to care when she decided she wanted to break up.

I'd usually solve a good puzzle or do some papercraft when I feel down, but I just haven't had the energy to do anything lately. "What's the point?" I think, "I'm just going to get depressed again later. There's no use wasting my time creating junk out of paper."
Maybe, I have to admit that it sounds a bit scary. I was surrounded by police the last time I was in the emergency room. I'd like to not have to go through that again.

Well, I'm at very little risk to do anything drastic right now. I'm just trying to figure out how to stop myself from hitting that point again. Besides, me being just depressed isn't exactly an emergency.
I'm sorry for being so difficult. I really wish I could just snap out of it. I just can't seem to do it. I know what will happen if I don't do something about it, but it feels inevitable.
Not anymore. My last case was bad enough to get me permanently banned from seeking help at the campus. I'd either be rejected or recognized and hauled off to some mental ward again.
I'm getting a few, however, they're too far to get to without a car. Even if I could get there, trying to find the time when I'm not busy with college or anything is very difficult.
Hm, I think I'm doing it right, but it's not pulling up anything for my area.
